# Task: A runner that Space starts and stops and that wraps around

Build a scene named Demo that looks and behaves as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 10) looking at the origin, with an orthographic projection whose visible height is 12.8 world units (near plane 0.1, far plane 1000); so one world unit is ten pixels.
- A thin dark grey track named Track: a box 12 wide, 0.2 high and 0.2 deep at (0, -1, 0), colour #404040.
- An orange block named Runner: a box 1 wide, 1 high and 0.5 deep, colour #f97316, starting at (-5, 0, 0). It starts stopped.
- A press of the Space bar toggles the Runner between stopped and moving. While it is moving it moves along +X at 4 world units per second of program time (program time is the sum of the frame durations the program is given; the distance covered in a frame is 4 times that frame's duration). While it is stopped it stays where it is, and starting it again continues from there.
- The Runner's x is kept in the range -6 <= x < 6: when moving takes it to 6 or beyond, 12 is subtracted, so it re-enters at the left.
All surfaces are flat colours (no lighting). Nothing else moves.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Runner, Track

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

# Reference: three.js r186 (WebGPU, TSL) and the project's support module

This document is the same for every task. It lists the API a project can rely on; every name in it was checked
against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

The project is TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) with one entry, `src/main.ts`, bundled for a browser.
It imports three.js from `three/webgpu` (all classes) and `three/tsl` (the node shading language) and the support module
from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

## The support module (`@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`)

```ts
type Vec3 = readonly [number, number, number];
function srgb(hex: string): Color;                       // "#rrggbb" sRGB colour -> three.js linear working colour
function unlit(hex: string): MeshBasicMaterial;          // flat colour, no lighting
function boxMesh(size: Vec3, material: Material): Mesh;  // full edge lengths along x, y, z
function sphereMesh(radius: number, material: Material, segments = 32, rings = 16): Mesh;
function lookAtCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; fovY?: number /* radians, full vertical, default 0.9 */; near?: number /* 0.1 */; far?: number /* 1000 */ }): PerspectiveCamera;  // square aspect
function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;
function startTask(build: (host: TaskHost) => TaskApp | Promise<TaskApp>): Promise<void>;

interface TaskHost {
  onKeyDown(code: string, handler: () => void): void;   // after the key went down
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
  isKeyDown(code: string): boolean;                     // as of the current frame
  onInput(name: string, handler: (value: unknown) => void): void; // declares a host input; the page sets it, the handler gets the value in the next frame's input phase
}
interface TaskApp {
  readonly scene: Scene;
  readonly camera: Camera;
  readonly clearColor: string;                          // "#rrggbb" (sRGB)
  fixedUpdate?(dt: number): void;                       // once per fixed tick, dt = 1/60
  update?(dt: number): void;                            // once per frame, dt in seconds (clamped to 0.1)
}

// Textures (an image the project provides as assets/<name>, loaded before the scene is built):
function loadTexture(url: string, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear" /* default srgb */; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): Promise<Texture>;
function configureTexture<T extends Texture>(texture: T, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear"; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): T;
// build may be async: `void startTask(async (host) => { const t = await loadTexture("assets/swatch.png", { filter: "nearest", wrap: "repeat" }); ... })`
```

The camera helpers and primitives use the defaults above; plain three.js objects work as well.

## three.js r186 essentials

Units are metres and radians; the coordinate system is right-handed with +Y up, the camera looks down -Z until it is
told otherwise; colours given as `"#rrggbb"` or hex numbers are sRGB and are converted to the linear working space
(`new Color(0x22c55e)`, `new Color().setStyle("#22c55e")`, or `srgb("#22c55e")`).

**Scene graph.** `Object3D` (base of `Scene`, `Group`, `Mesh`, lights, cameras): `name`, `position` (`Vector3`: `set(x,y,z)`,
`x`, `y`, `z`), `rotation` (`Euler`, radians, order XYZ: `rotation.y += a`), `quaternion`, `scale` (`Vector3`), `visible`,
`add(...children)`, `remove(...children)`, `children`, `parent`, `getObjectByName(name)`, `traverse(fn)`,
`lookAt(x, y, z)`, `rotateX/Y/Z(angle)`. A child's transform is relative to its parent; `new Group()` is an empty
node used to move several objects together.

**Meshes and geometry.** `new Mesh(geometry, material)`. Geometries (all dimensions are full sizes unless it says radius):
`BoxGeometry(width, height, depth)`, `SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments = 32, heightSegments = 16)`,
`PlaneGeometry(width, height)` (lies in the XY plane facing +Z; `rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2` lays it flat facing +Y),
`CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments)`, `ConeGeometry(radius, height, radialSegments)`,
`CircleGeometry(radius, segments)`, `TorusGeometry(radius, tube, radialSegments, tubularSegments)`.

**Materials.** `MeshBasicMaterial({ color, map?, side? })`: unlit flat colour. `MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness,
metalness, map? })`: physically based, needs lights. `material.color` is a `Color` (`material.color.set("#ff0000")`,
`.copy(srgb("#ff0000"))`, `.setRGB(r, g, b)` in linear values); `material.name` is a string; `material.map` a `Texture`;
`material.side` is `FrontSide` (default), `BackSide` or `DoubleSide`. A material is shared by every mesh that uses it.
Changing `color` of a built material takes effect on the next frame; nothing has to be rebuilt.

**Lights** (physical units): `AmbientLight(color, intensity)`; `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` shines from its
`position` toward its `target` (default the origin); `PointLight(color, intensity, distance = 0, decay = 2)` with
`distance` 0 meaning no range limit; `SpotLight`, `HemisphereLight` exist too. A matte surface of colour `albedo` facing a
point light of intensity `I` at distance `d` (decay 2) has the outgoing radiance `albedo * I / (pi * d * d)`; a surface
facing a directional light of intensity `E` squarely has `albedo * E / pi`; ambient light adds `albedo * intensity / pi`
(each multiplied by the light colour). Lights are `Object3D`s: add them to the scene.

**Cameras.** `PerspectiveCamera(fovDegrees, aspect, near, far)` (field of view in DEGREES, vertical), `OrthographicCamera(left, right,
top, bottom, near, far)`; place with `position.set(...)` and `lookAt(...)`.

**Math.** `Vector3` (`set`, `add`, `sub`, `multiplyScalar`, `length`, `normalize`, `lerp`, `clone`), `Color`, `Euler`,
`Quaternion` (`setFromAxisAngle(axis, angle)`), `MathUtils.degToRad`, `MathUtils.clamp`, `MathUtils.lerp`, `MathUtils.mapLinear`.

## TSL (`three/tsl`): shader logic as node expressions

A node material replaces fixed material parameters by node graphs; the shader is built once when the material is first
used, so animate through uniforms, not by replacing the material.

```ts
import { uniform, vec3, color, mix, sin, positionLocal, uv, texture, float, clamp, smoothstep } from "three/tsl";
import { MeshBasicNodeMaterial, MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu";

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";
material.colorNode = vec3(level);            // per-pixel colour; the result is displayed as it is
level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- Constructors: `float(x)`, `vec2(...)`, `vec3(...)` (`vec3(s)` fills all three), `vec4(...)`, `color(colorOrHex)`.
- Arithmetic on nodes: `a.add(b)`, `a.sub(b)`, `a.mul(b)`, `a.div(b)`, `a.oneMinus()`, `a.negate()`; numbers are accepted
  where a node is expected. Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, `v.xyz`.
- Functions (each also a method): `mix(a, b, t)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `smoothstep(lo, hi, x)`, `step(edge, x)`, `sin`, `cos`,
  `abs`, `pow`, `fract`, `min`, `max`, `length`, `normalize`, `dot`, `saturate`.
- Inputs: `positionLocal` (object-space position of the surface point, a vec3), `positionWorld`, `normalLocal`,
  `normalWorld`, `uv()` (texture coordinates, a vec2), `texture(tex, uv?)` (a sampled vec4), `time` (seconds of the
  renderer's own real-time clock, not of the application's frame clock).
- Node material slots: `colorNode` (base colour; for `MeshBasicNodeMaterial` the final colour), `opacityNode`, `roughnessNode`,
  `metalnessNode`, `emissiveNode` (on `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`).
- `color(c)` makes a colour node from a three.js `Color` (for an sRGB hex colour pass `srgb("#rrggbb")`). Node arithmetic on
  colours is done in linear light, and the result is displayed as it is.
- Conditionals: `select(condition, a, b)`; `If(cond, () => { ... })` inside `Fn(() => { ... })`.

## Conventions of the tests

Tests press keys, set host inputs, step frames of a given duration and compare pixels of the render target with
colours. Nothing else is observable: motion shows as pixels, state shows as colours. A project that does not type-check,
throws on start or writes to the console (errors or warnings) fails.

```
  scene: new Scene(),
  camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 1], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
  clearColor: "#000000",
}));
```

facing a directional light of intensity `E` squarely has `albedo * E / pi`; ambient light adds `albedo * intensity / pi`
(each multiplied by the light colour). Lights are `Object3D`s: add them to the scene.

## TSL (`three/tsl`): shader logic as node expressions

A node material replaces fixed material parameters by node graphs; the shader is built once when the material is first
used, so animate through uniforms, not by replacing the material.

```ts
import { uniform, vec3, color, mix, sin, positionLocal, uv, texture, float, clamp, smoothstep } from "three/tsl";

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";
material.colorNode = vec3(level);            // per-pixel colour; the result is displayed as it is
level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- Arithmetic on nodes: `a.add(b)`, `a.sub(b)`, `a.mul(b)`, `a.div(b)`, `a.oneMinus()`, `a.negate()`; numbers are accepted

- Conditionals: `select(condition, a, b)`; `If(cond, () => { ... })` inside `Fn(() => { ... })`.

# Task: A red ball on a floor lit by one point light

Build a scene named Demo that renders exactly as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #10131a.
- One camera at (0, 3, 8) looking at the point (0, 0.5, 0), with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.8 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- Both solids use a physically based material of the metallic-roughness kind, non-metallic (metalness 0), so they show a diffuse colour and a weak specular highlight:
  - A sphere named Ball centred at (0, 1, 0), radius 1.0, base colour #e11d48, roughness 0.7.
  - A flat square named Floor, 14 x 14 units, one-sided, facing up (+Y), lying in the plane y = 0 and centred on the origin, base colour #9aa5b1, roughness 0.9.
- One white point light named Lamp at (1.5, 3, 2.5) that shines equally in all directions, with no range limit. Its illumination falls off with the inverse square of the distance from the lamp, and its strength is calibrated so that a perfectly matte (Lambertian) white surface that is 3 units from the lamp and whose normal points straight at it renders as exactly white; a surface at an angle to the light receives proportionally less (the cosine of the angle).
- A white ambient light of 5% of that strength: it adds, to every surface and regardless of its orientation, 5% of the surface's own diffuse colour.
There are no shadows and no tone mapping: values above full brightness are simply clipped. The expected pixels were computed with the standard model (Lambertian diffuse plus a GGX specular term with Schlick Fresnel) and are checked with a tolerance of 6 per colour channel, which covers the small differences between implementations of that model (the shading of a tessellated sphere, rounding).

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Lamp, Floor, Ball

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

# Reference: three.js r186 (WebGPU, TSL) and the project's support module

against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };

```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

```ts

function srgb(hex: string): Color;                       // "#rrggbb" sRGB colour -> three.js linear working colour
function unlit(hex: string): MeshBasicMaterial;          // flat colour, no lighting
function boxMesh(size: Vec3, material: Material): Mesh;  // full edge lengths along x, y, z
function sphereMesh(radius: number, material: Material, segments = 32, rings = 16): Mesh;
function lookAtCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; fovY?: number /* radians, full vertical, default 0.9 */; near?: number /* 0.1 */; far?: number /* 1000 */ }): PerspectiveCamera;  // square aspect
function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;
function startTask(build: (host: TaskHost) => TaskApp | Promise<TaskApp>): Promise<void>;

interface TaskHost {
  onKeyDown(code: string, handler: () => void): void;   // after the key went down
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
  isKeyDown(code: string): boolean;                     // as of the current frame
  onInput(name: string, handler: (value: unknown) => void): void; // declares a host input; the page sets it, the handler gets the value in the next frame's input phase
}

  readonly scene: Scene;
  readonly camera: Camera;
```

```ts

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";

level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- The clear (background) colour is #1e293b.

- Six boxes, all with flat colours (no lighting), each with its own name. Edge length 2.0 in every direction unless stated:
  - Mid at (0, 0, 0): colour #ef4444.
  - Slab at (-2.5, 0, 5.5): colour #22c55e.
  - Far at (3.2, 0, -4): colour #3b82f6, edge length 3.0.
  - Behind at (0, 0, 14): colour #ec4899.
  - Ghost at (3, 0, 2): colour #facc15. It exists in the scene but is hidden: it must not be drawn.
  - Rim at (3.2, -2.2, 0): colour #a855f7, edge lengths 2.0 (x), 2.0 (y) and 5.0 (z).
Nothing special has to be programmed for the clipping: it is what the camera's near and far planes do to ordinary solid boxes. function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;

```ts
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
```

# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A box named Panel at (0.4, 0, 0), 4 wide (x), 2 high (y) and 0.2 deep (z), drawn with a custom material named Sweep. The surface is not lit. Its colour is computed for every pixel from x, the x coordinate of the surface point in the box's own object space (in metres, so it runs from -2 to 2 across the panel wherever the panel stands), and from t, the elapsed time in seconds: let w = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(0.8 * x + t); the colour is (1 - w) * A + w * B with A = #1a237e and B = #ffb300. The blend is done in linear light, on the two colours converted from sRGB to linear, and the result is displayed as it is.
- t is the elapsed time of the application: the sum of the durations of all the frames run so far, including the frame being drawn (after 16 frames of 0.0625 seconds each, t is 1). t must reach the material as a value that is updated every frame; the material and its shader are not replaced as time passes.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Panel, Sweep

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

messages.content:
# Task: A runner that Space starts and stops and that wraps around

Build a scene named Demo that looks and behaves as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 10) looking at the origin, with an orthographic projection whose visible height is 12.8 world units (near plane 0.1, far plane 1000); so one world unit is ten pixels.
- A thin dark grey track named Track: a box 12 wide, 0.2 high and 0.2 deep at (0, -1, 0), colour #404040.
- An orange block named Runner: a box 1 wide, 1 high and 0.5 deep, colour #f97316, starting at (-5, 0, 0). It starts stopped.
- A press of the Space bar toggles the Runner between stopped and moving. While it is moving it moves along +X at 4 world units per second of program time (program time is the sum of the frame durations the program is given; the distance covered in a frame is 4 times that frame's duration). While it is stopped it stays where it is, and starting it again continues from there.
- The Runner's x is kept in the range -6 <= x < 6: when moving takes it to 6 or beyond, 12 is subtracted, so it re-enters at the left.
All surfaces are flat colours (no lighting). Nothing else moves.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Runner, Track

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

# Reference: three.js r186 (WebGPU, TSL) and the project's support module

This document is the same for every task. It lists the API a project can rely on; every name in it was checked
against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

The project is TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) with one entry, `src/main.ts`, bundled for a browser.
It imports three.js from `three/webgpu` (all classes) and `three/tsl` (the node shading language) and the support module
from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

## The support module (`@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`)

```ts
type Vec3 = readonly [number, number, number];
function srgb(hex: string): Color;                       // "#rrggbb" sRGB colour -> three.js linear working colour
function unlit(hex: string): MeshBasicMaterial;          // flat colour, no lighting
function boxMesh(size: Vec3, material: Material): Mesh;  // full edge lengths along x, y, z
function sphereMesh(radius: number, material: Material, segments = 32, rings = 16): Mesh;
function lookAtCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; fovY?: number /* radians, full vertical, default 0.9 */; near?: number /* 0.1 */; far?: number /* 1000 */ }): PerspectiveCamera;  // square aspect
function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;
function startTask(build: (host: TaskHost) => TaskApp | Promise<TaskApp>): Promise<void>;

interface TaskHost {
  onKeyDown(code: string, handler: () => void): void;   // after the key went down
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
  isKeyDown(code: string): boolean;                     // as of the current frame
  onInput(name: string, handler: (value: unknown) => void): void; // declares a host input; the page sets it, the handler gets the value in the next frame's input phase
}
interface TaskApp {
  readonly scene: Scene;
  readonly camera: Camera;
  readonly clearColor: string;                          // "#rrggbb" (sRGB)
  fixedUpdate?(dt: number): void;                       // once per fixed tick, dt = 1/60
  update?(dt: number): void;                            // once per frame, dt in seconds (clamped to 0.1)
}

// Textures (an image the project provides as assets/<name>, loaded before the scene is built):
function loadTexture(url: string, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear" /* default srgb */; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): Promise<Texture>;
function configureTexture<T extends Texture>(texture: T, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear"; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): T;
// build may be async: `void startTask(async (host) => { const t = await loadTexture("assets/swatch.png", { filter: "nearest", wrap: "repeat" }); ... })`
```

The camera helpers and primitives use the defaults above; plain three.js objects work as well.

## three.js r186 essentials

Units are metres and radians; the coordinate system is right-handed with +Y up, the camera looks down -Z until it is
told otherwise; colours given as `"#rrggbb"` or hex numbers are sRGB and are converted to the linear working space
(`new Color(0x22c55e)`, `new Color().setStyle("#22c55e")`, or `srgb("#22c55e")`).

**Scene graph.** `Object3D` (base of `Scene`, `Group`, `Mesh`, lights, cameras): `name`, `position` (`Vector3`: `set(x,y,z)`,
`x`, `y`, `z`), `rotation` (`Euler`, radians, order XYZ: `rotation.y += a`), `quaternion`, `scale` (`Vector3`), `visible`,
`add(...children)`, `remove(...children)`, `children`, `parent`, `getObjectByName(name)`, `traverse(fn)`,
`lookAt(x, y, z)`, `rotateX/Y/Z(angle)`. A child's transform is relative to its parent; `new Group()` is an empty
node used to move several objects together.

**Meshes and geometry.** `new Mesh(geometry, material)`. Geometries (all dimensions are full sizes unless it says radius):
`BoxGeometry(width, height, depth)`, `SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments = 32, heightSegments = 16)`,
`PlaneGeometry(width, height)` (lies in the XY plane facing +Z; `rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2` lays it flat facing +Y),
`CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments)`, `ConeGeometry(radius, height, radialSegments)`,
`CircleGeometry(radius, segments)`, `TorusGeometry(radius, tube, radialSegments, tubularSegments)`.

**Materials.** `MeshBasicMaterial({ color, map?, side? })`: unlit flat colour. `MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness,
metalness, map? })`: physically based, needs lights. `material.color` is a `Color` (`material.color.set("#ff0000")`,
`.copy(srgb("#ff0000"))`, `.setRGB(r, g, b)` in linear values); `material.name` is a string; `material.map` a `Texture`;
`material.side` is `FrontSide` (default), `BackSide` or `DoubleSide`. A material is shared by every mesh that uses it.
Changing `color` of a built material takes effect on the next frame; nothing has to be rebuilt.

**Lights** (physical units): `AmbientLight(color, intensity)`; `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` shines from its
`position` toward its `target` (default the origin); `PointLight(color, intensity, distance = 0, decay = 2)` with
`distance` 0 meaning no range limit; `SpotLight`, `HemisphereLight` exist too. A matte surface of colour `albedo` facing a
point light of intensity `I` at distance `d` (decay 2) has the outgoing radiance `albedo * I / (pi * d * d)`; a surface
facing a directional light of intensity `E` squarely has `albedo * E / pi`; ambient light adds `albedo * intensity / pi`
(each multiplied by the light colour). Lights are `Object3D`s: add them to the scene.

**Cameras.** `PerspectiveCamera(fovDegrees, aspect, near, far)` (field of view in DEGREES, vertical), `OrthographicCamera(left, right,
top, bottom, near, far)`; place with `position.set(...)` and `lookAt(...)`.

**Math.** `Vector3` (`set`, `add`, `sub`, `multiplyScalar`, `length`, `normalize`, `lerp`, `clone`), `Color`, `Euler`,
`Quaternion` (`setFromAxisAngle(axis, angle)`), `MathUtils.degToRad`, `MathUtils.clamp`, `MathUtils.lerp`, `MathUtils.mapLinear`.

## TSL (`three/tsl`): shader logic as node expressions

A node material replaces fixed material parameters by node graphs; the shader is built once when the material is first
used, so animate through uniforms, not by replacing the material.

```ts
import { uniform, vec3, color, mix, sin, positionLocal, uv, texture, float, clamp, smoothstep } from "three/tsl";
import { MeshBasicNodeMaterial, MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu";

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";
material.colorNode = vec3(level);            // per-pixel colour; the result is displayed as it is
level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- Constructors: `float(x)`, `vec2(...)`, `vec3(...)` (`vec3(s)` fills all three), `vec4(...)`, `color(colorOrHex)`.
- Arithmetic on nodes: `a.add(b)`, `a.sub(b)`, `a.mul(b)`, `a.div(b)`, `a.oneMinus()`, `a.negate()`; numbers are accepted
  where a node is expected. Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, `v.xyz`.
- Functions (each also a method): `mix(a, b, t)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `smoothstep(lo, hi, x)`, `step(edge, x)`, `sin`, `cos`,
  `abs`, `pow`, `fract`, `min`, `max`, `length`, `normalize`, `dot`, `saturate`.
- Inputs: `positionLocal` (object-space position of the surface point, a vec3), `positionWorld`, `normalLocal`,
  `normalWorld`, `uv()` (texture coordinates, a vec2), `texture(tex, uv?)` (a sampled vec4), `time` (seconds of the
  renderer's own real-time clock, not of the application's frame clock).
- Node material slots: `colorNode` (base colour; for `MeshBasicNodeMaterial` the final colour), `opacityNode`, `roughnessNode`,
  `metalnessNode`, `emissiveNode` (on `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`).
- `color(c)` makes a colour node from a three.js `Color` (for an sRGB hex colour pass `srgb("#rrggbb")`). Node arithmetic on
  colours is done in linear light, and the result is displayed as it is.
- Conditionals: `select(condition, a, b)`; `If(cond, () => { ... })` inside `Fn(() => { ... })`.

## Conventions of the tests

Tests press keys, set host inputs, step frames of a given duration and compare pixels of the render target with
colours. Nothing else is observable: motion shows as pixels, state shows as colours. A project that does not type-check,
throws on start or writes to the console (errors or warnings) fails.

Looking at this code, I need to identify the off-by-one error in the loop that places markers.

The task states that each row should have exactly five markers at x positions: -3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, and 3.

Let me trace through the current loop:
```ts
for (let i = 1; i < COLUMNS; i += 1) {
  const marker = boxMesh([0.8, 0.8, 0.8], unlit("#facc15"));
  marker.name = "Marker";
  marker.position.set(SPACING * (i - 2), y, 0);
  scene.add(marker);
}
```

With `COLUMNS = 5` and `SPACING = 1.5`:
- i = 1: x = 1.5 * (1 - 2) = -1.5
- i = 2: x = 1.5 * (2 - 2) = 0
- i = 3: x = 1.5 * (3 - 2) = 1.5
- i = 4: x = 1.5 * (4 - 2) = 3

This only creates 4 markers, but we need 5! The loop condition `i < COLUMNS` should be `i <= COLUMNS` to include the case where i = 5:
- i = 5: x = 1.5 * (5 - 2) = 4.5

Wait, that would give x = 4.5, not -3. Let me reconsider.

Actually, with the formula `SPACING * (i - 2)` and needing x values of -3, -1.5, 0, 1.5, 3:
- For x = -3: i - 2 = -2, so i = 0
- For x = -1.5: i - 2 = -1, so i = 1
- For x = 0: i - 2 = 0, so i = 2
- For x = 1.5: i - 2 = 1, so i = 3
- For x = 3: i - 2 = 2, so i = 4

So the loop should run from i = 0 to i = 4 (inclusive), which means `for (let i = 0; i < COLUMNS; i += 1)` or `for (let i = 0; i <= 4; i += 1)`.

The current loop starts at `i = 1` and goes while `i < 5`, so it runs for i = 1, 2, 3, 4 (missing i = 0). This is the off-by-one error.

This document is the same for every task. It lists the API a project can rely on; every name in it was checked
against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

The project is TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) with one entry, `src/main.ts`, bundled for a browser.
It imports three.js from `three/webgpu` (all classes) and `three/tsl` (the node shading language) and the support module
from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

## The support module (`@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`)

```ts
type Vec3 = readonly [number, number, number];
function srgb(hex: string): Color;                       // "#rrggbb" sRGB colour -> three.js linear working colour
function unlit(hex: string): MeshBasicMaterial;          // flat colour, no lighting
function boxMesh(size: Vec3, material: Material): Mesh;  // full edge lengths along x, y, z
function sphereMesh(radius: number, material: Material, segments = 32, rings = 16): Mesh;
function lookAtCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; fovY?: number /* radians, full vertical, default 0.9 */; near?: number /* 0.1 */; far?: number /* 1000 */ }): PerspectiveCamera;  // square aspect
function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;
function startTask(build: (host: TaskHost) => TaskApp | Promise<TaskApp>): Promise<void>;

interface TaskHost {
  onKeyDown(code: string, handler: () => void): void;   // after the key went down
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
  isKeyDown(code: string): boolean;                     // as of the current frame
  onInput(name: string, handler: (value: unknown) => void): void; // declares a host input; the page sets it, the handler gets the value in the next frame's input phase
}
interface TaskApp {
  readonly scene: Scene;
  readonly camera: Camera;
  readonly clearColor: string;                          // "#rrggbb" (sRGB)
  fixedUpdate?(dt: number): void;                       // once per fixed tick, dt = 1/60
  update?(dt: number): void;                            // once per frame, dt in seconds (clamped to 0.1)
}

// Textures (an image the project provides as assets/<name>, loaded before the scene is built):
function loadTexture(url: string, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear" /* default srgb */; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): Promise<Texture>;
function configureTexture<T extends Texture>(texture: T, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear"; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): T;
// build may be async: `void startTask(async (host) => { const t = await loadTexture("assets/swatch.png", { filter: "nearest", wrap: "repeat" }); ... })`
```

The camera helpers and primitives use the defaults above; plain three.js objects work as well.

## three.js r186 essentials

Units are metres and radians; the coordinate system is right-handed with +Y up, the camera looks down -Z until it is
told otherwise; colours given as `"#rrggbb"` or hex numbers are sRGB and are converted to the linear working space
(`new Color(0x22c55e)`, `new Color().setStyle("#22c55e")`, or `srgb("#22c55e")`).

**Scene graph.** `Object3D` (base of `Scene`, `Group`, `Mesh`, lights, cameras): `name`, `position` (`Vector3`: `set(x,y,z)`,
`x`, `y`, `z`), `rotation` (`Euler`, radians, order XYZ: `rotation.y += a`), `quaternion`, `scale` (`Vector3`), `visible`,
`add(...children)`, `remove(...children)`, `children`, `parent`, `getObjectByName(name)`, `traverse(fn)`,
`lookAt(x, y, z)`, `rotateX/Y/Z(angle)`. A child's transform is relative to its parent; `new Group()` is an empty
node used to move several objects together.

**Meshes and geometry.** `new Mesh(geometry, material)`. Geometries (all dimensions are full sizes unless it says radius):
`BoxGeometry(width, height, depth)`, `SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments = 32, heightSegments = 16)`,
`PlaneGeometry(width, height)` (lies in the XY plane facing +Z; `rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2` lays it flat facing +Y),
`CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments)`, `ConeGeometry(radius, height, radialSegments)`,
`CircleGeometry(radius, segments)`, `TorusGeometry(radius, tube, radialSegments, tubularSegments)`.

**Materials.** `MeshBasicMaterial({ color, map?, side? })`: unlit flat colour. `MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness,
metalness, map? })`: physically based, needs lights. `material.color` is a `Color` (`material.color.set("#ff0000")`,
`.copy(srgb("#ff0000"))`, `.setRGB(r, g, b)` in linear values); `material.name` is a string; `material.map` a `Texture`;
`material.side` is `FrontSide` (default), `BackSide` or `DoubleSide`. A material is shared by every mesh that uses it.
Changing `color` of a built material takes effect on the next frame; nothing has to be rebuilt.

**Lights** (physical units): `AmbientLight(color, intensity)`; `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` shines from its
`position` toward its `target` (default the origin); `PointLight(color, intensity, distance = 0, decay = 2)` with
`distance` 0 meaning no range limit; `SpotLight`, `HemisphereLight` exist too. A matte surface of colour `albedo` facing a
point light of intensity `I` at distance `d` (decay 2) has the outgoing radiance `albedo * I / (pi * d * d)`; a surface
facing a directional light of intensity `E` squarely has `albedo * E / pi`; ambient light adds `albedo * intensity / pi`
(each multiplied by the light colour). Lights are `Object3D`s: add them to the scene.

**Cameras.** `PerspectiveCamera(fovDegrees, aspect, near, far)` (field of view in DEGREES, vertical), `OrthographicCamera(left, right,
top, bottom, near, far)`; place with `position.set(...)` and `lookAt(...)`.

**Math.** `Vector3` (`set`, `add`, `sub`, `multiplyScalar`, `length`, `normalize`, `lerp`, `clone`), `Color`, `Euler`,
`Quaternion` (`setFromAxisAngle(axis, angle)`), `MathUtils.degToRad`, `MathUtils.clamp`, `MathUtils.lerp`, `MathUtils.mapLinear`.

## TSL (`three/tsl`): shader logic as node expressions

A node material replaces fixed material parameters by node graphs; the shader is built once when the material is first
used, so animate through uniforms, not by replacing the material.

```ts
import { uniform, vec3, color, mix, sin, positionLocal, uv, texture, float, clamp, smoothstep } from "three/tsl";
import { MeshBasicNodeMaterial, MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu";

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";
material.colorNode = vec3(level);            // per-pixel colour; the result is displayed as it is
level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- Constructors: `float(x)`, `vec2(...)`, `vec3(...)` (`vec3(s)` fills all three), `vec4(...)`, `color(colorOrHex)`.
- Arithmetic on nodes: `a.add(b)`, `a.sub(b)`, `a.mul(b)`, `a.div(b)`, `a.oneMinus()`, `a.negate()`; numbers are accepted
  where a node is expected. Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, `v.xyz`.
- Functions (each also a method): `mix(a, b, t)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `smoothstep(lo, hi, x)`, `step(edge, x)`, `sin`, `cos`,
  `abs`, `pow`, `fract`, `min`, `max`, `length`, `normalize`, `dot`, `saturate`.
- Inputs: `positionLocal` (object-space position of the surface point, a vec3), `positionWorld`, `normalLocal`,
  `normalWorld`, `uv()` (texture coordinates, a vec2), `texture(tex, uv?)` (a sampled vec4), `time` (seconds of the
  renderer's own real-time clock, not of the application's frame clock).
- Node material slots: `colorNode` (base colour; for `MeshBasicNodeMaterial` the final colour), `opacityNode`, `roughnessNode`,
  `metalnessNode`, `emissiveNode` (on `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`).
- `color(c)` makes a colour node from a three.js `Color` (for an sRGB hex colour pass `srgb("#rrggbb")`). Node arithmetic on
  colours is done in linear light, and the result is displayed as it is.
- Conditionals: `select(condition, a, b)`; `If(cond, () => { ... })` inside `Fn(() => { ... })`.

## Conventions of the tests

Tests press keys, set host inputs, step frames of a given duration and compare pixels of the render target with
colours. Nothing else is observable: motion shows as pixels, state shows as colours. A project that does not type-check,
throws on start or writes to the console (errors or warnings) fails.

messages.content:
# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A box named Panel at (0.4, 0, 0), 4 wide (x), 2 high (y) and 0.2 deep (z), drawn with a custom material named Sweep. The surface is not lit. Its colour is computed for every pixel from x, the x coordinate of the surface point in the box's own object space (in metres, so it runs from -2 to 2 across the panel wherever the panel stands), and from t, the elapsed time in seconds: let w = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(0.8 * x + t); the colour is (1 - w) * A + w * B with A = #1a237e and B = #ffb300. The blend is done in linear light, on the two colours converted from sRGB to linear, and the result is displayed as it is.
- t is the elapsed time of the application: the sum of the durations of all the frames run so far, including the frame being drawn (after 16 frames of 0.0625 seconds each, t is 1). t must reach the material as a value that is updated every frame; the material and its shader are not replaced as time passes.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Panel, Sweep

messages.content:
# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A box named Panel at (0.4, 0, 0), 4 wide (x), 2 high (y) and 0.2 deep (z), drawn with a custom material named Sweep. The surface is not lit. Its colour is computed for every pixel from x, the x coordinate of the surface point in the box's own object space (in metres, so it runs from -2 to 2 across the panel wherever the panel stands), and from t, the elapsed time in seconds: let w = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(0.8 * x + t); the colour is (1 - w) * A + w * B with A = #1a237e and B = #ffb300. The blend is done in linear light, on the two colours converted from sRGB to linear, and the result is displayed as it is.
- t is the elapsed time of the application: the sum of the durations of all the frames run so far, including the frame being drawn (after 16 frames of 0.0625 seconds each, t is 1). t must reach the material as a value that is updated every frame; the material and its shader are not replaced as time passes.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Panel, Sweep

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

# Reference: three.js r186 (WebGPU, TSL) and the project's support module

This document is the same for every task. It lists the API a project can rely on; every name in it was checked
against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

The project is TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) with one entry, `src/main.ts`, bundled for a browser.
It imports three.js from `three/webgpu` (all classes) and `three/tsl` (the node shading language) and the support module
from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

## The support module (`@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`)

```ts
type Vec3 = readonly [number, number, number];
function srgb(hex: string): Color;                       // "#rrggbb" sRGB colour -> three.js linear working colour
function unlit(hex: string): MeshBasicMaterial;          // flat colour, no lighting
function boxMesh(size: Vec3, material: Material): Mesh;  // full edge lengths along x, y, z
function sphereMesh(radius: number, material: Material, segments = 32, rings = 16): Mesh;
function lookAtCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; fovY?: number /* radians, full vertical, default 0.9 */; near?: number /* 0.1 */; far?: number /* 1000 */ }): PerspectiveCamera;  // square aspect
function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;
function startTask(build: (host: TaskHost) => TaskApp | Promise<TaskApp>): Promise<void>;

interface TaskHost {
  onKeyDown(code: string, handler: () => void): void;   // after the key went down
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
  isKeyDown(code: string): boolean;                     // as of the current frame
  onInput(name: string, handler: (value: unknown) => void): void; // declares a host input; the page sets it, the handler gets the value in the next frame's input phase
}
interface TaskApp {
  readonly scene: Scene;
  readonly camera: Camera;
  readonly clearColor: string;                          // "#rrggbb" (sRGB)
  fixedUpdate?(dt: number): void;                       // once per fixed tick, dt = 1/60
  update?(dt: number): void;                            // once per frame, dt in seconds (clamped to 0.1)
}

// Textures (an image the project provides as assets/<name>, loaded before the scene is built):
function loadTexture(url: string, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear" /* default srgb */; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): Promise<Texture>;
function configureTexture<T extends Texture>(texture: T, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear"; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): T;
// build may be async: `void startTask(async (host) => { const t = await loadTexture("assets/swatch.png", { filter: "nearest", wrap: "repeat" }); ... })`
```

The camera helpers and primitives use the defaults above; plain three.js objects work as well.

## three.js r186 essentials

Units are metres and radians; the coordinate system is right-handed with +Y up, the camera looks down -Z until it is
told otherwise; colours given as `"#rrggbb"` or hex numbers are sRGB and are converted to the linear working space
(`new Color(0x22c55e)`, `new Color().setStyle("#22c55e")`, or `srgb("#22c55e")`).

**Scene graph.** `Object3D` (base of `Scene`, `Group`, `Mesh`, lights, cameras): `name`, `position` (`Vector3`: `set(x,y,z)`,
`x`, `y`, `z`), `rotation` (`Euler`, radians, order XYZ: `rotation.y += a`), `quaternion`, `scale` (`Vector3`), `visible`,
`add(...children)`, `remove(...children)`, `children`, `parent`, `getObjectByName(name)`, `traverse(fn)`,
`lookAt(x, y, z)`, `rotateX/Y/Z(angle)`. A child's transform is relative to its parent; `new Group()` is an empty
node used to move several objects together.

**Meshes and geometry.** `new Mesh(geometry, material)`. Geometries (all dimensions are full sizes unless it says radius):
`BoxGeometry(width, height, depth)`, `SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments = 32, heightSegments = 16)`,
`PlaneGeometry(width, height)` (lies in the XY plane facing +Z; `rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2` lays it flat facing +Y),
`CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments)`, `ConeGeometry(radius, height, radialSegments)`,
`CircleGeometry(radius, segments)`, `TorusGeometry(radius, tube, radialSegments, tubularSegments)`.

**Materials.** `MeshBasicMaterial({ color, map?, side? })`: unlit flat colour. `MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness,
metalness, map? })`: physically based, needs lights. `material.color` is a `Color` (`material.color.set("#ff0000")`,
`.copy(srgb("#ff0000"))`, `.setRGB(r, g, b)` in linear values); `material.name` is a string; `material.map` a `Texture`;
`material.side` is `FrontSide` (default), `BackSide` or `DoubleSide`. A material is shared by every mesh that uses it.
Changing `color` of a built material takes effect on the next frame; nothing has to be rebuilt.

**Lights** (physical units): `AmbientLight(color, intensity)`; `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` shines from its
`position` toward its `target` (default the origin); `PointLight(color, intensity, distance = 0, decay = 2)` with
`distance` 0 meaning no range limit; `SpotLight`, `HemisphereLight` exist too. A matte surface of colour `albedo` facing a
point light of intensity `I` at distance `d` (decay 2) has the outgoing radiance `albedo * I / (pi * d * d)`; a surface
facing a directional light of intensity `E` squarely has `albedo * E / pi`; ambient light adds `albedo * intensity / pi`
(each multiplied by the light colour). Lights are `Object3D`s: add them to the scene.

**Cameras.** `PerspectiveCamera(fovDegrees, aspect, near, far)` (field of view in DEGREES, vertical), `OrthographicCamera(left, right,
top, bottom, near, far)`; place with `position.set(...)` and `lookAt(...)`.

**Math.** `Vector3` (`set`, `add`, `sub`, `multiplyScalar`, `length`, `normalize`, `lerp`, `clone`), `Color`, `Euler`,
`Quaternion` (`setFromAxisAngle(axis, angle)`), `MathUtils.degToRad`, `MathUtils.clamp`, `MathUtils.lerp`, `MathUtils.mapLinear`.

## TSL (`three/tsl`): shader logic as node expressions

A node material replaces fixed material parameters by node graphs; the shader is built once when the material is first
used, so animate through uniforms, not by replacing the material.

```ts
import { uniform, vec3, color, mix, sin, positionLocal, uv, texture, float, clamp, smoothstep } from "three/tsl";
import { MeshBasicNodeMaterial, MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu";

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";
material.colorNode = vec3(level);            // per-pixel colour; the result is displayed as it is
level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- Constructors: `float(x)`, `vec2(...)`, `vec3(...)` (`vec3(s)` fills all three), `vec4(...)`, `color(colorOrHex)`.
- Arithmetic on nodes: `a.add(b)`, `a.sub(b)`, `a.mul(b)`, `a.div(b)`, `a.oneMinus()`, `a.negate()`; numbers are accepted
  where a node is expected. Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, `v.xyz`.
- Functions (each also a method): `mix(a, b, t)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `smoothstep(lo, hi, x)`, `step(edge, x)`, `sin`, `cos`,
  `abs`, `pow`, `fract`, `min`, `max`, `length`, `normalize`, `dot`, `saturate`.
- Inputs: `positionLocal` (object-space position of the surface point, a vec3), `positionWorld`, `normalLocal`,
  `normalWorld`, `uv()` (texture coordinates, a vec2), `texture(tex, uv?)` (a sampled vec4), `time` (seconds of the
  renderer's own real-time clock, not of the application's frame clock).
- Node material slots: `colorNode` (base colour; for `MeshBasicNodeMaterial` the final colour), `opacityNode`, `roughnessNode`,
  `metalnessNode`, `emissiveNode` (on `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`).
- `color(c)` makes a colour node from a three.js `Color` (for an sRGB hex colour pass `srgb("#rrggbb")`). Node arithmetic on
  colours is done in linear light, and the result is displayed as it is.
- Conditionals: `select(condition, a, b)`; `If(cond, () => { ... })` inside `Fn(() => { ... })`.

messages.content:
# Task: A runner that Space starts and stops and that wraps around

Build a scene named Demo that looks and behaves as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 10) looking at the origin, with an orthographic projection whose visible height is 12.8 world units (near plane 0.1, far plane 1000); so one world unit is ten pixels.
- A thin dark grey track named Track: a box 12 wide, 0.2 high and 0.2 deep at (0, -1, 0), colour #404040.
- An orange block named Runner: a box 1 wide, 1 high and 0.5 deep, colour #f97316, starting at (-5, 0, 0). It starts stopped.
- A press of the Space bar toggles the Runner between stopped and moving. While it is moving it moves along +X at 4 world units per second of program time (program time is the sum of the frame durations the program is given; the distance covered in a frame is 4 times that frame's duration). While it is stopped it stays where it is, and starting it again continues from there.
- The Runner's x is kept in the range -6 <= x < 6: when moving takes it to 6 or beyond, 12 is subtracted, so it re-enters at the left.
All surfaces are flat colours (no lighting). Nothing else moves.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Runner, Track

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

# Reference: three.js r186 (WebGPU, TSL) and the project's support module

This document is the same for every task. It lists the API a project can rely on; every name in it was checked
against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

The project is TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) with one entry, `src/main.ts`, bundled for a browser.
It imports three.js from `three/webgpu` (all classes) and `three/tsl` (the node shading language) and the support module
from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

## The support module (`@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`)

```ts
type Vec3 = readonly [number, number, number];
function srgb(hex: string): Color;                       // "#rrggbb" sRGB colour -> three.js linear working colour
function unlit(hex: string): MeshBasicMaterial;          // flat colour, no lighting
function boxMesh(size: Vec3, material: Material): Mesh;  // full edge lengths along x, y, z
function sphereMesh(radius: number, material: Material, segments = 32, rings = 16): Mesh;
function lookAtCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; fovY?: number /* radians, full vertical, default 0.9 */; near?: number /* 0.1 */; far?: number /* 1000 */ }): PerspectiveCamera;  // square aspect
function orthographicCamera(o: { position: Vec3; target: Vec3; height?: number /* visible world height = width, default 10 */; near?: number; far?: number }): OrthographicCamera;
function startTask(build: (host: TaskHost) => TaskApp | Promise<TaskApp>): Promise<void>;

interface TaskHost {
  onKeyDown(code: string, handler: () => void): void;   // after the key went down
  onKeyUp(code: string, handler: () => void): void;     // after the key went up
  isKeyDown(code: string): boolean;                     // as of the current frame
  onInput(name: string, handler: (value: unknown) => void): void; // declares a host input; the page sets it, the handler gets the value in the next frame's input phase
}
interface TaskApp {
  readonly scene: Scene;
  readonly camera: Camera;
  readonly clearColor: string;                          // "#rrggbb" (sRGB)
  fixedUpdate?(dt: number): void;                       // once per fixed tick, dt = 1/60
  update?(dt: number): void;                            // once per frame, dt in seconds (clamped to 0.1)
}

// Textures (an image the project provides as assets/<name>, loaded before the scene is built):
function loadTexture(url: string, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear" /* default srgb */; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): Promise<Texture>;
function configureTexture<T extends Texture>(texture: T, o: { colorSpace?: "srgb" | "linear"; filter: "nearest" | "linear"; wrap: "repeat" | "clamp" }): T;
// build may be async: `void startTask(async (host) => { const t = await loadTexture("assets/swatch.png", { filter: "nearest", wrap: "repeat" }); ... })`
```

The camera helpers and primitives use the defaults above; plain three.js objects work as well.

## three.js r186 essentials

Units are metres and radians; the coordinate system is right-handed with +Y up, the camera looks down -Z until it is
told otherwise; colours given as `"#rrggbb"` or hex numbers are sRGB and are converted to the linear working space
(`new Color(0x22c55e)`, `new Color().setStyle("#22c55e")`, or `srgb("#22c55e")`).

**Scene graph.** `Object3D` (base of `Scene`, `Group`, `Mesh`, lights, cameras): `name`, `position` (`Vector3`: `set(x,y,z)`,
`x`, `y`, `z`), `rotation` (`Euler`, radians, order XYZ: `rotation.y += a`), `quaternion`, `scale` (`Vector3`), `visible`,
`add(...children)`, `remove(...children)`, `children`, `parent`, `getObjectByName(name)`, `traverse(fn)`,
`lookAt(x, y, z)`, `rotateX/Y/Z(angle)`. A child's transform is relative to its parent; `new Group()` is an empty
node used to move several objects together.

**Meshes and geometry.** `new Mesh(geometry, material)`. Geometries (all dimensions are full sizes unless it says radius):
`BoxGeometry(width, height, depth)`, `SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments = 32, heightSegments = 16)`,
`PlaneGeometry(width, height)` (lies in the XY plane facing +Z; `rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2` lays it flat facing +Y),
`CylinderGeometry(radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments)`, `ConeGeometry(radius, height, radialSegments)`,
`CircleGeometry(radius, segments)`, `TorusGeometry(radius, tube, radialSegments, tubularSegments)`.

**Materials.** `MeshBasicMaterial({ color, map?, side? })`: unlit flat colour. `MeshStandardMaterial({ color, roughness,
metalness, map? })`: physically based, needs lights. `material.color` is a `Color` (`material.color.set("#ff0000")`,
`.copy(srgb("#ff0000"))`, `.setRGB(r, g, b)` in linear values); `material.name` is a string; `material.map` a `Texture`;
`material.side` is `FrontSide` (default), `BackSide` or `DoubleSide`. A material is shared by every mesh that uses it.
Changing `color` of a built material takes effect on the next frame; nothing has to be rebuilt.

**Lights** (physical units): `AmbientLight(color, intensity)`; `DirectionalLight(color, intensity)` shines from its
`position` toward its `target` (default the origin); `PointLight(color, intensity, distance = 0, decay = 2)` with
`distance` 0 meaning no range limit; `SpotLight`, `HemisphereLight` exist too. A matte surface of colour `albedo` facing a
point light of intensity `I` at distance `d` (decay 2) has the outgoing radiance `albedo * I / (pi * d * d)`; a surface
facing a directional light of intensity `E` squarely has `albedo * E / pi`; ambient light adds `albedo * intensity / pi`
(each multiplied by the light colour). Lights are `Object3D`s: add them to the scene.

**Cameras.** `PerspectiveCamera(fovDegrees, aspect, near, far)` (field of view in DEGREES, vertical), `OrthographicCamera(left, right,
top, bottom, near, far)`; place with `position.set(...)` and `lookAt(...)`.

**Math.** `Vector3` (`set`, `add`, `sub`, `multiplyScalar`, `length`, `normalize`, `lerp`, `clone`), `Color`, `Euler`,
`Quaternion` (`setFromAxisAngle(axis, angle)`), `MathUtils.degToRad`, `MathUtils.clamp`, `MathUtils.lerp`, `MathUtils.mapLinear`.

## TSL (`three/tsl`): shader logic as node expressions

A node material replaces fixed material parameters by node graphs; the shader is built once when the material is first
used, so animate through uniforms, not by replacing the material.

```ts
import { uniform, vec3, color, mix, sin, positionLocal, uv, texture, float, clamp, smoothstep } from "three/tsl";
import { MeshBasicNodeMaterial, MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu";

const level = uniform(0.25);                 // a node with a mutable `.value` (number, Color, Vector3, ...)
const material = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial(); // unlit; MeshStandardNodeMaterial for lit materials
material.name = "Shade";
material.colorNode = vec3(level);            // per-pixel colour; the result is displayed as it is
level.value = 0.5;                           // updates the shader's input, no rebuild
```

- Constructors: `float(x)`, `vec2(...)`, `vec3(...)` (`vec3(s)` fills all three), `vec4(...)`, `color(colorOrHex)`.
- Arithmetic on nodes: `a.add(b)`, `a.sub(b)`, `a.mul(b)`, `a.div(b)`, `a.oneMinus()`, `a.negate()`; numbers are accepted
  where a node is expected. Components: `v.x`, `v.y`, `v.z`, `v.xyz`.
- Functions (each also a method): `mix(a, b, t)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `smoothstep(lo, hi, x)`, `step(edge, x)`, `sin`, `cos`,
  `abs`, `pow`, `fract`, `min`, `max`, `length`, `normalize`, `dot`, `saturate`.
- Inputs: `positionLocal` (object-space position of the surface point, a vec3), `positionWorld`, `normalLocal`,
  `normalWorld`, `uv()` (texture coordinates, a vec2), `texture(tex, uv?)` (a sampled vec4), `time` (seconds of the
  renderer's own real-time clock, not of the application's frame clock).
- Node material slots: `colorNode` (base colour; for `MeshBasicNodeMaterial` the final colour), `opacityNode`, `roughnessNode`,
  `metalnessNode`, `emissiveNode` (on `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`).
- `color(c)` makes a colour node from a three.js `Color` (for an sRGB hex colour pass `srgb("#rrggbb")`). Node arithmetic on
  colours is done in linear light, and the result is displayed as it is.
- Conditionals: `select(condition, a, b)`; `If(cond, () => { ... })` inside `Fn(() => { ... })`.

## Conventions of the tests

Tests press keys, set host inputs, step frames of a given duration and compare pixels of the render target with
colours. Nothing else is observable: motion shows as pixels, state shows as colours. A project that does not type-check,
throws on start or writes to the console (errors or warnings) fails.

# Project files

## src/main.ts

```
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { lookAtCamera, startTask } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

// Skeleton. `startTask` renders the returned scene into a 128 x 128 target for the tests.
// Build the scene described in the task and return it.
void startTask(() => ({
  scene: new Scene(),
  camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 1], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
  clearColor: "#000000",
}));
```

# Task: A green box and a blue sphere on a dark grey background

Build a scene named Demo that renders exactly as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A green box named Cube at the origin: colour #22c55e, edge length 1.0.
- A blue sphere named Ball at (2, 0, 0), that is to the right of the box as seen from the camera: colour #3b82f6, radius 0.5.
All surfaces are flat colours (no lighting).

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Cube, Ball

# Reference documentation (three.js r186 and the project's support module)

# Reference: three.js r186 (WebGPU, TSL) and the project's support module

This document is the same for every task. It lists the API a project can rely on; every name in it was checked
against the installed packages (three 0.186.1).

## How a project works

The project is TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`) with one entry, `src/main.ts`, bundled for a browser.
It imports three.js from `three/webgpu` (all classes) and `three/tsl` (the node shading language) and the support module
from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the
render. Keys are named by `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"Space"`, `"KeyA"`, `"Enter"`, `"ArrowLeft"`).

Objects the task names are found by their `name` property (`mesh.name = "Cube"`, `material.name = "Sweep"`); give each
named thing exactly the name the task uses.

# Task: A cube and a floor lit by one directional light and an ambient term

Build a scene named Demo that renders exactly as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #0b0d12.
- One camera at (2.5, 2.5, 5) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- Both solids use a physically based material of the metallic-roughness kind, non-metallic (metalness 0), so they show a diffuse colour and a weak specular highlight:
  - A box named Cube centred at the origin, edge length 2.0, base colour #c8a27a, roughness 0.8.
  - A flat square named Floor, 10 x 10 units, one-sided, facing up (+Y), lying in the plane y = -1 and centred at (0, -1, 0), base colour #8a929c, roughness 0.9.
- One white directional light named Sun that travels in the direction (0, -0.6, -0.8) (that is, down and away from the camera). Its strength is calibrated so that a perfectly matte (Lambertian) white surface whose normal points straight at the light renders as exactly white; a surface at an angle to the light receives proportionally less (the cosine of the angle).
- A white ambient light of 10% of that strength: it adds, to every surface and regardless of its orientation, 10% of the surface's own diffuse colour.
There are no shadows and no tone mapping: values above full brightness are simply clipped. The expected pixels were computed with the standard model (Lambertian diffuse plus a GGX specular term with Schlick Fresnel) and are checked with a tolerance of 6 per colour channel, which covers the small differences between implementations of that model (the shading of a tessellated sphere, rounding).

# Task: A panel whose colour sweeps with time, computed in a custom material

Build a scene named Demo that renders as follows. The picture is square.
- The clear (background) colour is #202020.
- One camera at (0, 0, 6) looking at the origin, with a perspective projection (vertical field of view 0.9 radians, near plane 0.1, far plane 1000).
- A box named Panel at (0.4, 0, 0), 4 wide (x), 2 high (y) and 0.2 deep (z), drawn with a custom material named Sweep. The surface is not lit. Its colour is computed for every pixel from x, the x coordinate of the surface point in the box's own object space (in metres, so it runs from -2 to 2 across the panel wherever the panel stands), and from t, the elapsed time in seconds: let w = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(0.8 * x + t); the colour is (1 - w) * A + w * B with A = #1a237e and B = #ffb300. The blend is done in linear light, on the two colours converted from sRGB to linear, and the result is displayed as it is.
- t is the elapsed time of the application: the sum of the durations of all the frames run so far, including the frame being drawn (after 16 frames of 0.0625 seconds each, t is 1). t must reach the material as a value that is updated every frame; the material and its shader are not replaced as time passes.

These objects must exist when you are done, each with a three.js `name` (or material `name`) equal to the identifier: Panel, Sweep

from `@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support`. The entry calls `startTask` exactly once:

```ts
import { Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask, unlit } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

  const scene = new Scene();
  const cube = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], unlit("#22c55e"));
  cube.name = "Cube";
  scene.add(cube);
  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => { /* runs in the input phase of the next frame */ });
  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
    update(dt) { cube.rotation.y += dt; },
  };
});
```

`startTask` owns the renderer, a square 128 x 128 sRGB render target and the clock. Tests drive the application
frame by frame; the picture they read is the render target. A frame runs in this order: host inputs, key
transitions (down/up handlers), fixed ticks (`fixedUpdate`, 0 to 4 per frame of 1/60 s each), `update(dt)`, then the

import { uniform, vec3 } from "three/tsl";
import { MeshBasicNodeMaterial, Scene } from "three/webgpu";
import { boxMesh, lookAtCamera, startTask } from "@mtek/benchmarks/baseline-support";

void startTask((host) => {
  const scene = new Scene();

  // "Gauge": a node material that draws a flat grey whose linear light value is the uniform `level`.
  const level = uniform(0);
  const gauge = new MeshBasicNodeMaterial();
  gauge.name = "Gauge";
  gauge.colorNode = vec3(level);

  const meter = boxMesh([1, 1, 1], gauge);
  meter.name = "Meter";
  scene.add(meter);

  let charge = 0;

  host.onKeyDown("Space", () => {
    if (charge < 4) {
      charge += 1;
      level.value = charge / 4;
    }
  });

  host.onKeyDown("Backspace", () => {
    if (charge > 0) {
      charge -= 1;
      level.value = charge / 4;
    }
  });

  return {
    scene,
    camera: lookAtCamera({ position: [0, 0, 6], target: [0, 0, 0] }),
    clearColor: "#202020",
  };
});
>>>REPLACE
